title: Release gating + rollback switches for Dedicated Burst Capacity
creator: Talia Benson
body:
Context
- Dedicated Burst Capacity is rolling out behind feature gates and needs safe defaults + deterministic behavior under partial rollout.
- We need (1) feature flags for enabling burst, (2) config-level kill switches with immediate effect, (3) staged rollout gates by region/hardware, and (4) automated rollback triggers tied to non-burst SLOs.

Goals / deliverables
1) Layered gating model (hard -> soft)
- Hard off: global disable switch (fleet-wide). Must cut off burst admissions in <60s.
- Scoped off: region + hardware-class allow-list gate.
- Tenant gate: per-tenant enablement in control plane, with per-tenant caps.
- Request-level gate: admission controller decision based on pool health, fairness tokens, cooldown, etc.

2) Rollback switches
- Emergency kill switch (global) that can be flipped by SRE on-call without code deploy.
- Scoped kill switch (region/hardware) to isolate bad pools (e.g., eu-west L40S) without impacting other regions.
- “Soft rollback” mode: keep tenant enabled but force admission controller to return BURST_DENIED_* for all requests (preserves determinism + clear customer-facing denials).

3) Automated rollback criteria
- When non-burst tenant SLOs regress beyond thresholds for N minutes, automatically reduce/disable burst at the narrowest scope possible.
- Separate “safety circuit breaker” rollback when fleet caps exceeded or admission controller unhealthy.

Implementation plan
A) Switches + ownership
- Control plane config (source of truth):
  - burst.global_enabled (bool)
  - burst.global_mode (enum: ENABLED | DISABLED | FORCE_DENY)
  - burst.allowlist.region_hardware (string list like "us-east:h100", "eu-west:l40s")
  - burst.tenant_enabled (bool)
  - burst.tenant_priority_tier (string: gold|silver|standard)
- Runtime fast path:
  - Gateway/routing reads cached config snapshot (poll/stream) with max staleness budget.
  - Admission controller also reads same snapshot (or receives it via policy engine).
- On-call authority:
  - SRE can toggle burst.global_mode and burst.allowlist entries.
  - All changes are audit logged (see ENG-4870 / burst audit events doc).

B) Rollout stages (proposed)
- Stage 0 (dev): global_mode=DISABLED; allowlist empty.
- Stage 1 (staging): allowlist set to 1 region/hw; tenant_enabled only for internal tenant(s).
- Stage 2 (internal dogfood): allowlist expands to 2 regions/hw; tenant_enabled internal + 1 synthetic test tenant.
- Stage 3 (limited beta): allowlist expands per capacity plan; tenant_enabled for selected beta accounts only.
- Stage 4 (GA): allowlist for all GA-supported regions/hw; tenant_enabled via contract/package + provisioning workflow.

C) Automated rollback triggers
- Neighbor impact gate (non-burst protection):
  - Trigger if non-burst p95 latency increases > 8% vs trailing 24h baseline for 10 minutes AND overall error rate (5xx + timeouts) increases > 0.3% absolute.
  - Action: set burst.global_mode=FORCE_DENY for impacted scope (prefer region/hw scoped, else global), then page SRE.
- Fleet safety cap gate:
  - Trigger if burst_pool_utilization > 92% for 5 minutes AND queue_depth trend increasing (slope > threshold).
  - Action: set burst.global_mode=FORCE_DENY for that region/hw and alert (non-paging) unless non-burst SLO also regresses.
- Admission controller health gate:
  - Trigger if admission_controller p99 latency > 250ms for 5 minutes OR timeout rate > 0.5%.
  - Action: routing bypasses admission controller and treats all requests as BURST_DENIED_ADMISSION_UNAVAILABLE (deterministic) + flips scoped FORCE_DENY if persists > 15 minutes.
- Telemetry lag fairness gate:
  - Trigger if telemetry_lag_seconds > 30s p95 AND denial spikes correlate with lag.
  - Action: enable “telemetry smoothing” mode and cap effective burst ratio by 50% until lag subsides.

D) Observability / operational requirements
- Required dashboards for go/no-go:
  - burst_denials_total by reason (cardinality controlled)
  - nonburst_p95_latency_delta (by pool neighbor cohort)
  - admission_controller_errors/timeouts
  - global_mode changes (audit trail panel)
- Required alerts:
  - Page: non-burst SLO regression gate fired + burst still enabled
  - Page: admission controller timeouts causing routing fallback > threshold
  - Ticket: sustained pool saturation w/ rising queue

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Feature flags exist for global + region/hw + tenant.
- [x] Kill switch updates propagate to routing + admission decisions within 60 seconds.
- [x] Rollback mode is deterministic: same request under same snapshot results in same deny behavior (no flapping).
- [x] Automated rollback writes an auditable config change with actor="system" and includes triggering metrics snapshot.
- [x] Load test demonstrates rollback triggers fire and reduce neighbor impact (see ENG-4841).
- [x] Runbook updated to include switch locations + expected customer-facing behavior.

Notes / links
- Related PRs (expected):
  - sources/github/redwood/pr-23837-add-feature-flags-and-kill-switch-for-burst.json
  - sources/github/redwood/pr-23988-add-slo-gate-to-disable-burst-when-nonburst-latency-regresses.json
  - sources/github/redwood/pr-24074-rollout-toggle-by-region-and-hardware-class.json
  - sources/github/redwood/pr-23919-global-circuit-breaker-for-burst-pools.json
- Design references:
  - sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/burst-pool-architecture-and-guardrails.json
  - sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-burst-pool-admission-control-semantics.json
- SLO policy:
  - sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/dedicated-burst-slos-and-alerting.json

Open questions (resolved)
- Q: Should rollback be "hard" (disable) or "soft" (force deny with reason)?
  - Decision: default to FORCE_DENY (soft) for customer debuggability and to preserve deterministic denial codes; keep DISABLED for full shutdown.
- Q: Who is allowed to toggle global_mode?
  - Decision: SRE on-call + Infra lead; audited; write requires reason string.

Test plan
- Unit: policy engine evaluation for gating precedence.
- Integration: simulated config propagation delays (ensure max staleness behavior is safe).
- Game day: flip scoped kill switch while traffic ongoing; confirm customer sees consistent BURST_DENIED_* and baseline remains stable.

Rollout checklist
- Before enabling any beta tenant:
  - Validate allowlist contains only provisioned pools.
  - Confirm alerts are installed and paging routes are correct.
  - Confirm rollback automation has permission to write config + is rate limited.
- During beta:
  - Daily review of non-burst latency delta panels.
  - Verify no audit log gaps for config changes.
- Before GA:
  - Document the customer-visible semantics (retry guidance, 429 vs deny reasons) and align with Support tooling (ENG-4881).
comments: 2025-03-14 (Talia Benson): Creating as P0 — we can’t start beta without a kill switch + gates. Peter to own with Sean as reviewer for alerting/rollback semantics.

2025-03-18 (Peter Holtz): Drafted gating hierarchy (global -> region/hw -> tenant -> admission). Key ask: rollback should be FORCE_DENY (soft) so routing returns explicit BURST_DENIED_* instead of mysterious timeouts. Syncing with Mina/Ravi on routing behavior.

2025-03-25 (Mina Haddad): Routing can treat admission controller unavailable as deterministic deny, but we need a config snapshot version field to avoid flapping across instances. Please ensure we emit the snapshot_version in request logs for support debug.

2025-03-28 (Sean Gallagher): For automated rollback: gate must use non-burst SLO metrics only, not burst tenant metrics. We should page only if rollback fires AND regression persists after rollback (avoid noisy pages).

2025-04-02 (Jordan Lee): Added precedence rules to policy engine: DISABLED > FORCE_DENY > allowlist > tenant. Determinism note: snapshot must include allowlist + global_mode; do not read allowlist from two places.
2025-04-09 (Peter Holtz): Implemented scoped allowlist by region/hardware and wired into config cache. Working through propagation SLA; targeting <60s with watcher + fallback poll.
2025-04-16 (Allison Grant): Please keep alert label cardinality low: region, hardware_class, mode, reason_code only. No tenant_id on paging alerts (can be in dashboards).

2025-04-19 (Peter Holtz): Landed PR for feature flags/kill switch + allowlist gate. Next: SLO regression gate automation and runbook steps. Coordinating with ENG-4902 circuit breaker semantics to avoid conflicting actions.

2025-04-28 (Rafael Mendes): Game day ask: include scenario where automated rollback writes config but routing cache lags. We need a manual override procedure in runbook: how to force cache refresh / verify switch took effect.

2025-05-06 (Peter Holtz): SLO regression gate merged; added ‘system’ actor and embedded metric snapshot in audit event payload (stringified). Verified in staging that rollback toggles within ~35s median.

2025-05-13 (Sean Gallagher): Sign-off: rollback actions prefer scoped region/hw; global only if metrics are global or scope resolution fails. Paging rules updated per above (page on persistent regression).
2025-05-21 (Talia Benson): Marking Done. Requirements satisfied for internal beta entry. Follow-ups tracked in ENG-4862 (game day execution) and ENG-4881 (support playbook + denial code guidance).
